subject: Order Form: pricing protector clause / redline request
messages:
From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@acerohealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acerohealth.com>; procurement@acerohealth.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft order form — question on pricing protector

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for sending the updated order form. Procurement flagged the new pricing exhibits (Exhibit B — Fee Schedule) and asked us to propose a short "Price Protector" clause that prevents retroactive increases to the effective per-token rate within the first 12 months, unless there is mutual written agreement.

We don't object to floors/caps for volume true-ups, but we need clarity on how the floor gets applied if Redwood re-tiers pricing mid-year. Can Redwood put in a narrow redline that guarantees no unilateral price increase to committed unit pricing for 12 months after signature, with carve-outs for material changes (e.g., change in region or material regulatory costs) that would require notice?

I've attached the procurement team's suggested language as a PDF. Can your legal team take a look and propose counter-language if needed? We hope to sign the order next week.

Best,
Sarah Nguyen
Head of Procurement, AceroHealth
Attachments: Acero_PriceProtector_Suggested.pdf (pdf)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@acerohealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 10:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft order form — question on pricing protector

Sarah —

Thanks for the note and the suggested language. Appreciate the clarity around the 12-month window. Internal quick take: Redwood is comfortable committing to no unilateral increases to the committed per-token rate for 12 months post-signature so long as true-up mechanics and the cap/floor exhibit remain intact. Two asks from our side:

- We need an explicit carve-out allowing adjustment if AceroHealth requests deployment into a higher-cost region (we'll call this out as "Region Change").
- We also need to preserve our right to adjust ancillary fees (e.g., on-demand overage rates) with 30 days' notice; customers get the same notice.

I looped in Aditya (legal) and Laura (revops) to draft a short redline. I can send a nonbinding commercial note to keep momentum while legal polishes language.

Short next steps: Aditya will propose a concrete redline and attach it to the order form. If that looks good to you, we'll move to signature.

—Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0172

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 08:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Redwood proposed redline — Price Protector (clean + marked)

Sarah / AceroHealth team,

Attached is our proposed redline to cover the pricing protector you requested. For clarity, the redline does two things:

1) Commits to no increase to the "Committed Unit Price" set forth in Exhibit B for a period of 12 months following Effective Date, subject to the Region Change carve-out and material regulatory cost pass-throughs.
2) Confirms that the floor/cap mechanics in Exhibit B continue to operate for true-ups and volume tiers; those mechanics may result in post-commit adjustments but will not be characterized as unilateral increases to the committed per-unit rate within the 12-month window.

Key points we added in the redline (high level):
- Region Change: customer-requested deployment into a different cloud region that materially changes vendor costs (we set a bright-line of a >15% incremental infra cost) allows a negotiated adjustment with good-faith discussions.
- Overage Fee Notice: ancillary or on-demand overage fees may be adjusted with 30 days' notice; the committed unit price is insulated for the 12-month period.
- Mutual Remedies: if there is a dispute about whether a change qualifies as a Region Change, parties agree to escalation to execs for 7 business days prior to invoking adjustability.

I've attached: Acero_OrderForm_v3.docx (clean) and PriceProtector_Redline.pdf (marked). Please confirm any specific redline points you can't accept and we'll try to accommodate.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acerohealth.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@acerohealth.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 11:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed redline — Price Protector (clean + marked)

Aditya / Marissa,

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Two quick responses from our counsel here:

1) The Region Change carve-out is broadly acceptable, but we want the trigger to be narrower — suggest tying to actual billed infrastructure cost evidenced by invoice-level delta rather than a 15%% threshold. Procurement prefers objective, auditable triggers.

2) The mutual remedies / exec-escalation step is fine, but we'd like an automatic cap on potential post-adjustment increases to 10% in any 12-month period to avoid open-ended exposure.

We'll flag the exact language in our counter-markup and upload early tomorrow. Looking to close this week if possible.

—Tom
VP, Vendor Relations, AceroHealth

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acerohealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 09:25:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Redwood proposed redline — Price Protector (clean + marked)

Tom —

Appreciate the specificity. Our counter on your two points:

1) Objective trigger: happy to accept invoice-level delta as the supporting evidence for a Region Change, provided the supporting invoices show >15% incremental infra spend attributable uniquely to the change in deployment region. The combination gives both objectivity and a bright-line.

2) Cap on adjustments: we can accept an annualized cap of 12% on any price adjustment arising from the Region Change or regulatory pass-throughs, provided the cap is applied to the component of pricing impacted (e.g., infra-only component), and not to bundled discounts on committed rate. We cannot accept an unrestricted 10% cap across all levers because that could undermine our ability to recover genuine cost changes.

If that sounds workable I recommend we add a short phrase to Exhibit B and the Price Protector addendum: "Adjustments under the Region Change and regulatory pass-through carve-outs shall be evidenced by invoice-level deltas and shall not exceed twelve percent (12%) per 12-month period to the affected pricing components."

Marissa, Laura, Rishi — if we agree, please finalize the marked PDF and send to Acero for signature. I'll prepare a short commercial note describing the cap mechanics for their procurement team.

—Aditya

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah@acerohealth.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood proposed redline — Price Protector (clean + marked)

Marissa / Aditya —

We reviewed Aditya's suggested compromise internally and procurement is comfortable with the invoice-delta approach plus a 12% cap on the affected components. We will accept the revised language as final. Please send the signed order form (Exhibit B + Price Protector addendum) and we'll route for countersignature.

Two small operational asks before signature:
- Please confirm how true-ups will be calculated on monthly vs quarterly billing (we prefer quarterly).
- Please add a field in the order form indicating the "committed unit price" explicitly next to each tier for clarity.

If you can get the final docs out by EOD tomorrow, we'll execute on our side the same day.

Thanks — looking forward to working together.

Best,
Sarah
